teams.heading: Jake White takes charge of Fiji after two decades away from internationals
teams.body: Jake White is back coaching at international level after a 20-year gap, taking charge of Fiji with the 2007 World Cup on his résumé. "I've not coached at international level for 20 years, but I was very excited today," he said after the Japan win. Eddie Jones is his technical adviser, and White's Europe-based players should be available for the three Nations Championship games against France, Ireland and Italy.

lead.why: It is a different story from the Japan result and the World Cup quote already run on this tab, and it covers White's appointment itself.

teams.heading: Fin Baxter back from long layoff in Harlequins' 33-15 win over Saracens
teams.body: Fin Baxter's return to the pitch came in Harlequins' 33-15 win over Saracens, and it was a notable one for England. Planet Rugby described his first outing after a long injury layoff as one where "it really didn't look like he'd been out of the game for 10 months." He made a strong carry, won a scrum penalty in his first pack-down and went off at half-time, as expected. Baxter is also in Steve Borthwick's 36-man squad, named on Sunday for the November Nations Championship camp.

lead.why: The only genuinely new England item in the pack that isn't already covered in this tab's recent editions, since the Marchant and Randall stories have both run.

teams.heading: Cros says France lost 2023 quarter-final to Springboks in preparation
teams.body: Francois Cros has said France lost the 2023 World Cup quarter-final against South Africa before a ball was kicked, blaming preparation rather than the 80 minutes. The Toulouse loose forward, who came off the bench in the 29-28 defeat, said the Springboks were more physical and that France "were equally as good, if not better" on individual skill. He has never watched the game back. Next month's Stade de France meeting with South Africa offers that chance.

lead.why: A fresh interview with Cros on the 2023 quarter-final gives France fans a new angle ahead of next month's Springboks match, and it is not the Ward eligibility story already run.

teams.heading: Italy's best world ranking is No. 8, reached in 2007 and 2024
teams.body: Italy's best position in the world rankings is No. 8, reached in 2007 and again in 2024. The current log tells a harder story: after three matches they are 11 of 12, with no wins, three defeats, 37 points scored and 131 conceded, a points difference of -94. The most recent of those games was a 10-57 loss to Australia in Round three. Italy's next match is South Africa in Round four.

teams.heading: Stuart Hogg stripped of MBE after domestic abuse conviction, register confirms
teams.body: Former Scotland captain Stuart Hogg has had his MBE removed, with the Cabinet Office's official register confirming the revocation was made in March after his domestic abuse conviction. Hogg, who won 100 caps for Scotland and toured three times with the British & Irish Lions, pleaded guilty to a domestic abuse charge involving his estranged wife, Gillian, and received a one-year community payback order in January 2025. The honour had been awarded in the 2024 New Year Honours for services to rugby.

lead.why: It is the one fresh item not already reported on this tab, and it concerns a former Scotland captain's honour.

teams.heading: Reuben Morgan-Williams scores two tries in Ospreys' 31-14 derby win over Dragons
teams.body: Reuben Morgan-Williams scored two tries as the Ospreys beat the Dragons 31-14 at the newly developed St Helen's on Saturday, a performance that strengthens his case for a Wales place. WalesOnline's ratings gave him an 8 out of 10, the highest mark in the piece, and noted he heads into Wales camp with a chance to establish himself in the matchday 23.

teams.heading: Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast's wrist injury raises doubt for Argentina Test
teams.body: Ireland's fly-half picture is the open question before the November meeting with Argentina. RTÉ Sport reported that a wrist injury has made Sam Prendergast a doubt, and Irish coverage has since described it as a major injury scare, with his absence from a Munster match also reported. No clarification of his fitness has been reported yet. Contepomi names his November squad after the London camp, which runs Monday to Wednesday.

teams.heading: Les Kiss starts Declan Meredith at fly-half in Bledisloe shake-up
teams.body: Kiss made four changes to the starting XV for the second Bledisloe Cup Test, the most notable being Declan Meredith's selection at fly-half, as Australia's long search for a first-choice No. 10 continues. Australia's last result was a 21-43 loss to New Zealand, and a first win over the All Blacks since 2020 was the prize on offer. Rugby World's preview said even a narrow defeat would be a sign of progress.

teams.heading: Jake White's Japan debut ends 28-34 defeat to Fiji at centenary Test
teams.body: Jake White's first match in charge ended in a 28-34 defeat to Fiji in Saturday's centenary Test, with Ben Volavola's two late penalties settling it. Japan were level 21-21 at half-time and Warner Dearns scored twice, but the new coach admitted he was "excited and relieved" after a short time working with the squad. He now has a tough European tour against France, Ireland and Italy ahead.

lead.why: Jake White's first match in charge is a fresh coaching angle on the Fiji result, and the only Japan item in the shortlist that isn't already reported or about another team.

teams.heading: Sonny Bill Williams reveals open-heart surgery after heart defect found during neck follow-up
teams.body: Sonny Bill Williams has revealed he underwent open-heart surgery after a serious heart defect he was born with was found during a follow-up appointment for neck surgery. In an emotional YouTube video made with his wife Alana, the former All Blacks centre, who won two Rugby World Cup titles and made 58 Test appearances, said doctors called it a miracle the defect was caught, describing a condition that can strike a perfectly fit-looking person. The operation at Royal Melbourne Hospital was a success, he said.

lead.why: It is the strongest new New Zealand-linked item in the pack; the injury list is already reported and the other new item concerns an Argentina player.
